newsitem.title: MALI: Mali bans marches on eve of election protest.
newsitem.headline: Mali bans marches on eve of election protest.

text.p: Mali's government banned all street protests ahead of a planned opposition demonstration on Wednesday to demand fresh elections after a chaotic weekend parliamentary poll.
Territorial Administration and Security Minister Lieutenant-Colonel Sada Samake announced the move in a statement issued on Tuesday.

Earlier, officials from two opposition alliances urged their supporters to turn out in force on Wednesday to demonstrate their rejection of Sunday's election which was dogged by organisational glitches which prevented many people voting.

The poll for a new 147-seat national assembly and presidential and municipal elections in May and June are a test of how deeply democracy has taken root in Mali, which won widespread praise for its 1992 democratic transition from military dictatorship.

Voters turned out in force for the election, which launched the impoverished nation's second multi-party national polls since independence from France in 1960. They cited problems with voter cards and electoral lists and lack of voting materials.

The opposition alliances has called for the election process to be suspended and reorganised. They have also demanded the resignation of President Alpha Oumar Konare's government for failing to arrange proper polling.

Konare, a historian elected in 1992, is due to face nine challengers in a May 4 presidential poll. He has steered Mali on a course of economic liberalisation, winning praise from the United States and the World Bank.
